intro:
The best home theater for Samsung smart TV owners is the [Samsung HW-Q990F](/gear/samsung-hw-q990f/), an 11.1.4-channel soundbar system with a wireless subwoofer and up-firing rear speakers in the box, plus Q-Symphony to blend your TV's speakers into the mix. This page is for anyone with a Samsung TV (or about to buy one) who wants to know which Samsung sound system fits their room, and when a receiver or another brand makes more sense.

We cover Samsung's two flagship soundbars and its two best OLED TVs for a home theater, explain Q-Symphony and wireless Dolby Atmos in plain terms, and flag the compatibility catches, including DTS. Rankings are built on Samsung's spec sheets and owner reports, not lab benches.
quickAnswer: The best home theater for a Samsung smart TV is the HW-Q990F: 11.1.4 channels, Dolby Atmos and DTS:X, a wireless sub and rears included, and Q-Symphony so the TV speakers play along. On a tighter budget, the HW-Q800F gives you 5.1.2 with a sub. If you are choosing the TV too, the S95F is the best Samsung TV for home theater, and the S90F is the value pick.
picksHeading: The Samsung Home Theater Lineup, Ranked

picks.body:
**Why it wins:** The HW-Q990F is the most complete soundbar system any brand sells in one box. Samsung rates it at **11.1.4 channels**: the main bar, a **wireless subwoofer** and **two wireless rear speakers with their own up-firing drivers**, so height effects come from behind you as well as in front. It decodes both [Dolby Atmos](/glossary/dolby-atmos/) and [DTS:X](/glossary/dts-x/), something Bose and Sonos bars cannot do.

With a recent Samsung TV, **Q-Symphony** adds the TV's speakers to the mix, and **wireless Dolby Atmos** lets the TV send Atmos to the bar over Wi-Fi with no HDMI cable. SpaceFit Sound Pro calibrates the system for your room, and Active Voice Amplifier Pro raises dialogue when background noise rises.

**Do the maths:** this whole system sits in roughly the **$1,500–$2,000** band. A Bose Smart Ultra with bass module and surrounds costs more, and a Sonos Arc Ultra with Sub 4 and Era 300s costs much more, and neither includes DTS:X or rear height channels at this price.

**The trade-off:** the rears and sub each need a power outlet, and Q-Symphony and wireless Atmos only work with Samsung TVs. Bass is strong for a soundbar system but will not match a dedicated 12-inch sub in a large room.

**Who it suits:** almost any Samsung TV owner with a medium or large living room. Against the HW-Q800F below, you gain rear speakers and six more channels.

**Why it wins:** The HW-Q800F gives you most of what makes Samsung's soundbars good for well under Q990F money, in roughly the **$700–$1,000** band. It is a **5.1.2-channel** system with up-firing drivers in the bar and a **wireless subwoofer** in the box, and it keeps Dolby Atmos and DTS:X decoding, Q-Symphony, wireless Dolby Atmos from compatible Samsung TVs and SpaceFit Sound Pro calibration.

The included sub is the key difference from rivals at this price. Sonos's Beam (Gen 2) and Bose's Smart Soundbar ship without one, and adding a Sonos or Bose sub costs about as much again. For films, a bar with a sub beats a bigger bar without one in most living rooms.

**The trade-off:** no rear speakers. Surround effects are simulated from the front, which works for TV and streaming but is less convincing with action films. Samsung sells wireless rear speaker kits that add real surrounds later.

**Who it suits:** Samsung TV owners with 55 to 65-inch screens in small and medium rooms, and anyone who wants Atmos and a sub without stretching to the Q990F. Compared with the Q990F above, you give up the rears and six channels but save roughly half. Against the [Sony Bravia Theater Bar 8](/gear/sony-bravia-theater-bar-8/), the Samsung includes a sub and integrates with Samsung TVs; the Sony integrates with Bravias instead.

picks.award: Best Samsung TV for Home Theater
picks.body:
**Why it wins:** If you are building a home theater around a Samsung TV, the S95F is the one to get. It uses a **QD-OLED** panel with Samsung's **glare-free matte coating**, which matters in living rooms with windows and lamps: reflections that would wash out a glossy OLED are diffused instead. OLED's per-pixel lighting gives you perfect blacks for films in a dark room.

For a home theater hub, check the connections. It has **four [HDMI 2.1](/glossary/hdmi-2-1/) ports**, so a console, streaming box and Blu-ray player can all run at full quality, and an [eARC](/glossary/earc/) port for your soundbar or receiver. It supports [HDR](/glossary/hdr/) in HDR10, HDR10+ and HLG, with high refresh rates for gaming. It also unlocks Q-Symphony and wireless Dolby Atmos with the Q990F and Q800F.

**The trade-off:** no Dolby Vision. Samsung backs HDR10+ instead, so Dolby Vision content plays in standard HDR10. Most viewers will not notice, but it matters to some film fans. It is also a premium-priced TV.

**Who it suits:** film fans and gamers who want the best Samsung picture in a bright or mixed-light room. Against the S90F below, you get the glare-free screen and more brightness. Against Sony's [Bravia 8 II](/gear/sony-bravia-8-ii/), the Sony offers Dolby Vision and Acoustic Center Sync; the Samsung offers the matte screen and Q-Symphony. See our [best TV for home theater](/best-tv-for-home-theater/) roundup for more.

picks.award: Best Value Samsung TV for Home Theater
picks.body:
**Why it wins:** The S90F gives you OLED contrast, Samsung's full smart platform and the same home theater connections as the S95F for noticeably less. It has **four HDMI 2.1 ports**, eARC, HDR10, HDR10+ and HLG support, and full Q-Symphony and wireless Dolby Atmos support with Samsung soundbars.

Depending on screen size and region, S90F panels come from either Samsung Display (QD-OLED) or LG Display (WOLED). Owners report both look excellent in dark rooms, but if you care about the panel type, check the exact model and size before buying.

**The trade-off:** a glossy screen and lower brightness than the S95F. In a bright room with windows facing the TV, reflections are more visible. Like every Samsung TV, there is no Dolby Vision.

**Who it suits:** most people building a home theater around a Samsung TV, especially in a room you can darken for movies. Use our [viewing distance calculator](/tools/viewing-distance-calculator/) to pick the size: for a 9-foot seating distance, a 65-inch screen fills about 30 degrees of your view, which is close to the common recommendation for mixed TV and film viewing. Compared with the S95F above, you give up the anti-glare coating and some brightness. Against the [LG C5](/gear/lg-c5-oled/), the Samsung adds HDR10+ and Q-Symphony; the LG adds Dolby Vision.

sections.heading: The Short Verdict
sections.body:
For a Samsung TV, a Samsung soundbar is the easiest high-quality upgrade. The [HW-Q990F](/gear/samsung-hw-q990f/) is the best value complete system on the market: a bar, sub and up-firing rears with DTS:X for less than a comparable Bose or Sonos build. The [HW-Q800F](/gear/samsung-hw-q800f/) is the right pick for smaller rooms and budgets.

Samsung's integration features, Q-Symphony and wireless Dolby Atmos, are genuinely useful, but they are a bonus rather than a requirement. Any Samsung TV with eARC also works well with an AV receiver or another brand's soundbar.

The catches: Samsung TVs do not support Dolby Vision, and their DTS support has been patchy over the years, so connect disc players to the soundbar or receiver directly if you rely on DTS soundtracks. If you are still choosing a TV, the [S95F](/gear/samsung-s95f/) is the best Samsung for a home theater and the [S90F](/gear/samsung-s90f/) is the value pick.

sections.heading: Who Samsung Is
sections.body:
Samsung Electronics has been the world's best-selling TV brand for well over a decade, and it has turned that lead into a full home theater ecosystem. Its soundbars are tuned at Samsung's US-based Audio Lab, and since 2017 Samsung has owned **Harman**, the parent of JBL, Harman Kardon and Infinity. That is why Harman Kardon branding has appeared on some Samsung soundbars, and why JBL's soundbars, such as the [JBL Bar 1300MK2](/gear/jbl-bar-1300mk2/), are the closest outside alternative.

Samsung's home theater range is built around soundbars rather than receivers or passive speakers. The Q-series runs from compact bars to the flagship Q990F, and Samsung sells wireless rear kits and subwoofers to expand them. On the TV side, Samsung sells Neo QLED (Mini LED) and OLED models, all running its Tizen smart platform with the SmartThings app.

See all Samsung products we cover on our [Samsung brand page](/brands/samsung/).

sections.heading: Building the Best Home Theater for Samsung Smart TV Owners
sections.body:
The best home theater for a Samsung smart TV depends on your room and how much you want to run cables. Here are the four realistic paths:

| Path | What you buy | Best for |
|---|---|---|
| Complete soundbar system | HW-Q990F | Most living rooms; best value full surround |
| Bar + sub | HW-Q800F | Small to medium rooms, tighter budgets |
| Another brand's soundbar | Sonos, Sony or Bose | Multiroom music, or brand preference |
| Receiver + speakers | AVR + passive speakers | Biggest output, full upgrade path |

**Size the bar to the TV.** A 55-inch TV is about 48 inches wide, a 65-inch about 57 inches and a 77-inch about 67 inches. Big Samsung bars suit 65 inches and up.

**Size the system to the room.** In a room under about 2,000 cubic feet (for example 12 x 15 x 8 ft = 1,440 cu ft), the Q800F with its sub is enough. In larger rooms, the Q990F's rear speakers make a big difference, because sound from behind you does not depend on bouncing off distant side walls.

**Connect it correctly.** Use the TV's HDMI eARC port, then set the TV's sound output to the soundbar or receiver over HDMI eARC, turn on Anynet+ (HDMI-CEC) so one remote controls both, and set digital audio output to passthrough or auto. For wireless Dolby Atmos, connect the bar and TV to the same Wi-Fi network through the SmartThings app; for lossless soundtracks from discs, a wired eARC connection is still the safer choice.

sections.heading: How Q-Symphony and Wireless Dolby Atmos Work
sections.body:
**Q-Symphony** lets a compatible Samsung TV and Samsung soundbar play at the same time instead of muting the TV speakers. The TV's speakers take on part of the sound, mainly the center and height layer around the screen, so voices and effects seem to come from the picture rather than below it. Owners report it widens the front soundstage, especially on larger TVs. It works over HDMI eARC, optical or Wi-Fi, depending on the model pairing.

**Wireless Dolby Atmos** lets recent Samsung TVs send Atmos audio to the Q990F or Q800F over Wi-Fi. That is useful if you wall-mount the TV and do not want an HDMI cable running down to the bar. The trade-off is that wireless connections carry the streaming versions of Atmos, so for lossless Dolby TrueHD from Blu-ray, use the HDMI eARC cable.

**Compatibility.** Both features need a Samsung TV and a Samsung soundbar from compatible model years. Most current Samsung OLED and Neo QLED TVs support them with the Q990F and Q800F. Check Samsung's compatibility list for older TVs. Neither feature works with non-Samsung TVs, but the bars themselves work with any TV over HDMI or optical.

sections.heading: Using a Receiver With a Samsung Smart TV
sections.body:
If you want the most output and the freedom to upgrade one speaker at a time, the best home theater receiver for a Samsung smart TV is any current AVR with eARC and good room correction. Our picks:

- **[Denon AVR-X1800H](/gear/denon-avr-x1800h/):** seven channels for 5.1.2, Audyssey room correction and eARC. The best value for most systems.
- **[Denon AVR-X2800H](/gear/denon-avr-x2800h/):** more power and features for medium rooms.
- **[Yamaha RX-V6A](/gear/yamaha-rx-v6a/):** seven channels with YPAO correction and a clean app.
- **[Sony STR-AN1000](/gear/sony-str-an1000/):** a strong alternative with 360 Spatial Sound Mapping.

**What to prioritize.** Samsung TVs do not output Dolby Vision, so you do not need a receiver with Dolby Vision passthrough for the TV itself. Connect consoles directly to the TV's HDMI 2.1 ports for 4K/120 gaming and let eARC send the audio back to the receiver. Connect your Blu-ray player directly to the receiver so DTS:X and Dolby TrueHD soundtracks reach it untouched, whatever the TV's own DTS support.

Pair the receiver with a speaker package such as the [Klipsch Reference Theater Pack](/gear/klipsch-reference-theater-pack/) or [Polk T-Series 5.1 system](/gear/polk-t-series-51-system/). See our [best home theater receiver](/best-home-theater-receiver/) guide for more.

sections.heading: Best Equalizer Settings for Samsung Home Theater
sections.body:
Samsung soundbars sound best with a light touch. Start here:

- **Run SpaceFit Sound Pro first.** Let it calibrate the bar for your room before touching the EQ.
- **Sound mode:** Adaptive Sound for TV and mixed content, Surround for films without Atmos, Standard for music, and Game mode for consoles.
- **EQ:** in the SmartThings app, start flat. If dialogue is hard to hear, raise the upper-mid bands slightly rather than lowering bass.
- **Subwoofer level:** start at zero and adjust one step at a time. Too much bass masks dialogue.
- **Center level:** raise it one or two steps if voices get lost; this is often better than using a voice mode.
- **Active Voice Amplifier Pro:** useful in noisy rooms, but turn it off for films.
- **Night mode:** compresses loud effects for late-night viewing.

On the TV, set sound output to the soundbar, turn on Q-Symphony if available, and avoid TV-side sound effects; let the bar do the processing.

sections.heading: What Samsung Does Well
sections.body:
**Value.** The Q990F gives you more channels, DTS:X and rear speakers for less than comparable Bose or Sonos systems.

**Integration.** Q-Symphony, wireless Dolby Atmos and one-remote control make the TV and soundbar feel like one product.

**Formats.** Samsung bars decode both Dolby Atmos and DTS:X.

**Included subs.** Both the Q990F and Q800F ship with a wireless subwoofer, so you do not pay extra for bass.

**TV choice.** Samsung's OLEDs combine excellent contrast with four HDMI 2.1 ports, and the S95F's glare-free screen is a real advantage in bright rooms.

sections.heading: Where Samsung Falls Short
sections.body:
**No Dolby Vision on Samsung TVs.** Samsung uses HDR10+ instead. Content mastered in Dolby Vision plays in HDR10.

**Patchy DTS history.** Samsung TVs dropped DTS decoding for several years, and passthrough support varies by model. Disc fans should connect players to the soundbar or receiver directly.

**Best features need Samsung on both ends.** Q-Symphony and wireless Atmos do not work with other TV or soundbar brands.

**Less multiroom.** Samsung bars support streaming and AirPlay on many models, but nothing close to Sonos's whole-home system.

**Bass limits.** The included subs are good for soundbar systems, but a receiver with a dedicated 12-inch sub will dig deeper in large rooms. See our [best subwoofer for home theater](/best-subwoofer-for-home-theater/) guide.

sections.heading: Samsung vs Sonos, Sony and LG
sections.body:
**Samsung vs Sonos:** the Q990F costs much less than the full Sonos Arc Ultra, Sub 4 and Era 300 system, and adds DTS:X. Sonos wins on multiroom music and app polish. See our [Sonos home theater review](/sonos-home-theater-review/).

**Samsung vs Sony:** Sony's Bravia Theater Bar 9 also decodes DTS:X and uses Acoustic Center Sync with Bravia TVs, but it ships without a sub or rears. If your TV is a Samsung, the Q990F is the better buy. See our [Sony home theater review](/sony-home-theater-review/).

**Samsung vs LG:** on TVs, the [LG C5](/gear/lg-c5-oled/) and [LG C6](/gear/lg-c6-oled/) support Dolby Vision, which Samsung's do not; Samsung's S95F counters with its glare-free screen. Either brand works well with any soundbar or receiver over eARC.

**Samsung vs Bose:** Bose has the better dialogue mode and design, but costs more for fewer channels and no DTS:X. See our [Bose home theater review](/bose-home-theater-review/).

sections.heading: Who Should Skip Samsung
sections.body:
- **Dolby Vision fans choosing a TV.** Look at LG or Sony instead.
- **Owners of non-Samsung TVs who want TV integration.** Q-Symphony will not work; pick a soundbar that matches your TV brand, or choose purely on sound.
- **Multiroom music fans.** Sonos is the stronger platform.
- **Big-room movie fans.** A receiver with passive speakers and a dedicated sub scales further. Start with our [best home theater systems](/best-home-theater-systems/) roundup.

We ranked these four products using Samsung's published specs, room maths and owner-reported reliability, not lab benches.

mistakes.title: Plugging into the wrong HDMI port
mistakes.body: Only one HDMI port on a Samsung TV supports eARC, and it is labeled. Connect the soundbar or receiver there, or Dolby Atmos and lossless audio will not pass through.

mistakes.title: Leaving TV audio set to PCM
mistakes.body: If the TV's digital audio output is set to PCM, the bar receives a downmixed signal. Set it to passthrough or auto so Atmos and DTS reach the soundbar.

mistakes.title: Relying on the TV for DTS discs
mistakes.body: Samsung TVs have patchy DTS support. Connect your Blu-ray player to the soundbar's HDMI input, where it has one, or to a receiver so DTS:X soundtracks arrive untouched.

mistakes.title: Turning everything up in the EQ
mistakes.body: Boosting bass and treble together mostly adds distortion. Run SpaceFit Sound Pro, keep the EQ near flat, and adjust center and sub levels instead.

mistakes.title: Ignoring rear speaker power
mistakes.body: The Q990F's rear speakers and sub are wireless but still need power outlets. Plan their positions before you buy so cables stay tidy.

faqs.q: What is the best home theater system for a Samsung smart TV?
faqs.a: The Samsung HW-Q990F is the best home theater system for most Samsung smart TVs. It includes a soundbar, wireless subwoofer and up-firing rear speakers for 11.1.4 channels, decodes Dolby Atmos and DTS:X, and works with Q-Symphony and wireless Dolby Atmos on compatible Samsung TVs.

Q-Symphony is a Samsung feature that lets a compatible Samsung TV's speakers play together with a Samsung soundbar instead of muting. The TV handles part of the sound around the screen, which widens the front soundstage and lifts dialogue toward the picture. It needs a Samsung TV and soundbar from compatible model years.

faqs.q: Do Samsung soundbars work with other TV brands?
faqs.a: Yes. Samsung soundbars connect to any TV over HDMI eARC, HDMI ARC or optical, and Dolby Atmos and DTS:X still work if the TV passes them through. You lose Q-Symphony and wireless Dolby Atmos, which need a Samsung TV, but room calibration and every sound mode still work.

faqs.q: Can I use a non-Samsung soundbar with a Samsung TV?
faqs.a: Yes. Any soundbar or AV receiver with HDMI eARC works with a recent Samsung TV, including Sonos, Sony, Bose and JBL models. You lose Q-Symphony, but you still get Dolby Atmos over eARC. Samsung TVs have patchy DTS support, so connect disc players to the soundbar or receiver directly.

It depends on the model and year. Samsung TVs dropped built-in DTS decoding for several years, and passthrough support has varied since. If you own Blu-rays with DTS or DTS:X soundtracks, connect the player directly to your soundbar or receiver rather than relying on the TV.

faqs.q: What is the best Samsung TV for home theater?
faqs.a: The Samsung S95F is the best Samsung TV for home theater, with a QD-OLED panel, a glare-free matte screen, four HDMI 2.1 ports and eARC. The S90F is the better value, with the same connections and OLED contrast but a glossy screen. Neither supports Dolby Vision; both support HDR10+.

faqs.q: Is the flagship Samsung soundbar system worth it over the cheaper model?
faqs.a: Yes, if your room is medium or large. The Q990F adds two wireless rear speakers with up-firing drivers, giving you real surround and overhead effects from behind. In a small room or on a tight budget, the Q800F with its included sub covers most of what matters.

bottomLine: The best home theater for a Samsung smart TV is the [HW-Q990F](/gear/samsung-hw-q990f/), which puts a bar, sub and up-firing rears with DTS:X in one box for less than rival systems; smaller rooms and budgets should choose the [HW-Q800F](/gear/samsung-hw-q800f/). If you are buying the TV too, the [S95F](/gear/samsung-s95f/) is the best Samsung for home theater and the [S90F](/gear/samsung-s90f/) is the value pick. Just remember the two catches, no Dolby Vision and patchy DTS on the TV side, and connect disc players to the soundbar or a receiver.
